=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/clarify_informal_detect.py
  Line or code reference: lines 80-110 (stdin reader with timeout)
  Problem: The stdin read path uses a daemon thread with a 5-second timeout. On timeout, a `TimeoutError` is raised and caught by the outer `except Exception:` handler in `main()`, which emits `PARSE_ERROR_OUTPUT` and returns 0. There is no warning or distinguishment between a genuine parse error and a timeout; the timeout path silently produces the same `signals=parse_error` output as an actual failure. The clarify prompt also does not list `parse_error` as a possible signal.
  Why it fails at runtime: A pipeline that feeds a large issue body through a slow pipe gets `CLARIFY_INFORMAL_SCORE: 0.000; signals=parse_error` indistinguishable from a genuine read failure. The clarify prompt also does not list `parse_error` as a possible signal, so the clarify model has no way to know the score is missing rather than genuinely zero.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/repo_root.py
  Line or code reference: lines 39-48 (`_has_git_marker` GIT_WORK_TREE fallback)
  Problem: The GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_DIR fallback only handles absolute `GIT_WORK_TREE` paths; relative `GIT_WORK_TREE` values are silently rejected with `return False`, which causes the function to fall through to the parent-walk. Some CI environments set relative `GIT_WORK_TREE` values that are valid when interpreted by git itself.
  Why it fails at runtime: In CI workspaces with relative `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `repo_root_from()` may exhaust MAX_PARENT_STEPS (10) and raise a RuntimeError, even though the repo is validly structured.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- File: scripts/generate_codex_model_reference.py
  Line or code reference: lines 155-190 (render_markdown loop)
  Problem: Duplicate-slug detection uses `slug in known_slugs` where `known_slugs` is a list, making the per-model membership check O(n) and the overall loop O(n²). Later, `set(known_slugs)` is constructed for the unknown-override check, which duplicates the conversion work.
  Why it fails at runtime: The current catalog has ~20 models so this is not a runtime problem today, but the quadratic growth pattern is gratuitous and will slow down CI drift checks as the catalog expands. A companion `set` for membership checks would keep the loop linear.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py
  Line or code reference: lines 160-161 (expand_source_glob(...) error message)
  Problem: The error message hard-codes `tools/repo_tree/config.yaml`, but `run()` supports an overridden `repo_root` parameter that can change the config file location.
  Why it fails at runtime: When a test or non-standard invocation passes a different `repo_root`, the error message in the raised exception references the wrong config path, misleading debugging.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: tests/fixtures/informal_issues/empty_body.json
  Line or code reference: line 1 (filename) and test name `test_empty_body_fixture_matches_expected_output`
  Problem: The fixture file is named `empty_body.json` and the corresponding test is named `test_empty_body_fixture_matches_expected_output`, but the fixture body contains "see attached log\nhttps://ex.org/x" — not an empty body. The fixture description says "Minimal issue body with a short log note and exactly one URL."
  Why it fails at runtime: This does not cause a runtime failure; the tests pass correctly. The name mismatch is misleading for maintainers reading test failures or adding new fixtures, who would reasonably expect `empty_body.json` to contain an empty string.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
